headline_marked: World Bank [[approves $1.1 billion emergency financing]] for Bangladesh
headline: World Bank approves $1.1 billion emergency financing for Bangladesh
summary: The funding aims to secure food supplies, support vulnerable households, and manage economic shocks caused by rising global prices.
details: The World Bank has approved $1.1 billion in emergency financing for Bangladesh to combat the impact of rising fertilizer, fuel, and food prices driven by the West Asia conflict.
The package consists of two main projects. $300 million is allocated to the Emergency Support for Food Security Project to import 600,000 metric tons of fertilizer for upcoming rice seasons.
This initiative will support rice cultivation across 1.4 million hectares of farmland, addressing the country's vulnerability as it imports over 85% of its fertilizer requirements.

The remaining $713 million will be provided under the Contingent Emergency Response Project to fund emergency expenditures, including cash transfers and livelihood support for affected households and small businesses.
This portion of the funding will also help sustain essential services such as healthcare, electricity, water supplies, and food distribution by funding necessary fuel and energy imports.
Jean Pesme, the World Bank's division director for Bangladesh and Bhutan, noted that tighter fiscal space and rising costs have deeply affected smallholder farmers and vulnerable households.
Bangladesh is also seeking additional external financing from other development partners, including the IMF, to shore up foreign exchange reserves and ease pressure on public finances.

The World Bank has approved $1.1 billion in emergency funds to protect Bangladesh's food security and vulnerable households.

The package consists of two main projects. $300 million is allocated to the Emergency Support for Food Security Project to import 600,000 metric tons of fertilizer for upcoming rice seasons.

This initiative will support rice cultivation across 1.4 million hectares of farmland, addressing the country's vulnerability as it imports over 85% of its fertilizer requirements.

The remaining $713 million will be provided under the Contingent Emergency Response Project to fund emergency expenditures, including cash transfers and livelihood support for affected households and small businesses.

This portion of the funding will also help sustain essential services such as healthcare, electricity, water supplies, and food distribution by funding necessary fuel and energy imports.

Jean Pesme, the World Bank's division director for Bangladesh and Bhutan, noted that tighter fiscal space and rising costs have deeply affected smallholder farmers and vulnerable households.

Bangladesh is also seeking additional external financing from other development partners, including the IMF, to shore up foreign exchange reserves and ease pressure on public finances.

headline: 43 sacks of cash found as Pagla Mosque's 13 donation boxes opened
summary: The mosque's donation boxes, opened after six months, contained a record amount of cash, gold jewelry, and foreign currency.
details: After six months, the 13 donation boxes of the Pagla Mosque were opened, revealing a massive amount of donations.
The collection included 43 sacks of cash, along with various gold ornaments and foreign currencies.
Authorities are currently in the process of counting the total amount collected.
This volume of donations is being described as a record amount for the mosque.
